_note: v2 hook overrides for la Banque du Village (B10_banque). Source hooks are kept where the painting shows them; these replace hooks whose painted scene differs, mostly to avoid text in the paintings and repeated motifs across the thirteen rooms.

fr_cheque_noun.hook: "SHEHK" ≈ "SHAKE": a man SHAKES hands with the teller and slides a big paper CHEQUE across the counter.

fr_solde_noun_m.hook: "SOLD": a clerk bangs her big rubber stamp on a slip, SOLD!, and checks the BALANCE that is left on a little brass balance scale. (Also: les soldes = the SALES.)
fr_solde_noun_m.why: No letters are painted (no text in the paintings), so the stamp and the little balance scale carry the hook.

fr_reputation_noun.hook: Like English 'reputation', said ray-pew-tah-SYOHN: a proud lady wears a shining gold star on her coat while her neighbours bow to her: her good REPUTATION.
fr_reputation_noun.why: Painted as a lady with the star rather than a banker, because the bank already has several men in suits.

fr_consommation_noun.hook: Like English 'consumption', said kohn-soh-mah-SYOHN: a basket of groceries hangs beside a tall thermometer gauge on the wall showing how much everyone CONSUMES.
fr_consommation_noun.why: Painted as a grocery basket with a thermometer gauge instead of a brass shopping-bag dial.

fr_epingle_noun.hook: "ay-PANG" ≈ "a PING!": an old tailor pushes a giant round-headed PIN through the red rosette on his apron: PING!
fr_epingle_noun.why: The pin has a big round head, so nothing sharp is shown.

fr_sou_noun.hook: "SOO" ≈ "SUE": little SUE drops a tiny copper SOU coin into a money box: her very last penny.
fr_sou_noun.why: Matches the painting: a money box on the floor instead of a slot in the wall.

fr_profil_noun.hook: "proh-FEEL" ≈ "PRO FEEL": on a board, the shadow of a silhouette artist in a beret runs his finger round the edge of a lady's black paper PROFILE to FEEL it.
fr_profil_noun.why: The artist appears as a black silhouette on the board next to the profile.

fr_portefeuille_noun.hook: "por-tuh-FUHY" ≈ "PORT a FOIL": a man in a mustard suit opens his leather WALLET, crammed with notes crinkly as FOIL.
fr_portefeuille_noun.why: The notes are painted plainly, so the foil is only in the words.

fr_acces_noun.hook: "ahk-SEH" ≈ "unLOCK, SAY!" (and it looks like English "access"): the little guard boy holds up a big brass KEY, the padlock on the garden gate hangs open, and he swings the gate wide: ACCESS granted.
fr_acces_noun.why: Owner rule: no weapons, so the toy axe is gone; the hook now rests on the key and padlock (unLOCK-say) plus the English cognate.

fr_gage_noun.hook: "GAHZH" ≈ "GARAGE": a boy kneels to hand over his toy GARAGE as a PLEDGE until he pays back what he owes.
fr_gage_noun.why: There is no pawn desk; the boy hands the toy garage to a smaller child.

fr_transfert_noun.hook: Like English 'transfer', said trahns-FEHR: a little FERRY carries one huge gold coin across the river from one bank to the other: a TRANSFER.
fr_transfert_noun.why: A real river seen through the window instead of a model river.

fr_centime_noun.hook: "sahn-TEEM" ≈ "SON TIM": little TIM rolls one giant copper CENT along the riverside path like a wheel.
fr_centime_noun.why: Painted on the path outside, not on the parquet.

fr_enjeu_noun.hook: "ahn-ZHEUH" ≈ "ON JEU (game)": two chess players hold up a gold coin over the board: the STAKE of the game.
fr_enjeu_noun.why: Matches the painting: the coin is held over the board.

fr_paiement_noun.hook: "peh-MAHN" ≈ "PAY, MAN!": a smiling woman holds out her cupped hands, "PAY, MAN!", and the PAYMENT drops into them coin by coin.
fr_paiement_noun.why: The coins fall into her hands from above; no second customer is painted.

fr_bancaire_adj.hook: "BANK CARE" ("bahn-KEHR"): a shiny gold BANK card hangs in a gilt frame on the window post, with a feather duster below to dust it with great CARE: all things BANKING.
fr_bancaire_adj.why: The card hangs on the window mullion, and it is blank (no text).

fr_emprunt_noun.hook: "ahn-PRUN" ≈ "on PRUNE": a granny signs a LOAN for a cart heaped with PRUNES: the borrowed money buys the PRUNES.
fr_emprunt_noun.why: A granny instead of a farmer, so the farmers are not repeated (one leads the goat in the placements office).

fr_debit_noun.hook: "day-BEE" ≈ "DEBBIE": little DEBBIE times the water gushing from a big brass tap with her stopwatch: the FLOW rate. (Also a bank DEBIT.)
fr_debit_noun.why: A girl called Debbie instead of a bee, because the bees already do le bilan.

fr_allocation_noun.hook: Like English 'allocation', said ah-loh-kah-SYOHN: a clerk ALLOCATES one gold coin into each tin of a long row.
fr_allocation_noun.why: The tins are plain (no labels), because the paintings hold no text.

fr_notoriete_noun.hook: "noh-toh-RYAY-tay" ≈ "NOTARY-TEA": a famous wigged NOTARY sips TEA while admiring fans crowd round him with their papers: such RENOWN.
fr_notoriete_noun.why: Matches the painting: the fans hold papers to be signed.

fr_contre_courant_noun.hook: "KOHN-truh koo-RAHN" ≈ "CONTRA-CURRENT": a salmon leaps AGAINST THE CURRENT up the stream of the office fountain.
fr_contre_courant_noun.why: The fountain stands inside the loans office, not in a courtyard.

fr_denomination_noun.hook: Like English 'denomination', said day-noh-mee-nah-SYOHN: a girl sorts banknotes into piles by colour and size: one pile for each DENOMINATION.
fr_denomination_noun.why: Sorted by colour and size, with no numbers, because the paintings hold no text.

fr_promotion_noun.hook: Like English 'promotion', said proh-moh-SYOHN: a shopkeeper in a tall cone hat, shaped like a megaphone, shouts a PROMOTION and swings a giant blank price tag.
fr_promotion_noun.why: The cone hat stands in for the megaphone, and the tag is blank.

fr_revenu_noun.hook: "ruh-vuh-NEW" ≈ "REVENUE": a baker carries the day's INCOME home in a bag of coins.
fr_revenu_noun.why: The bag is plain, without a sticker.

fr_lot_noun.hook: "LOH" ≈ "LOW": a girl surveyor marks out a LOW-fenced PLOT of land, one LOT among many.
fr_lot_noun.why: A girl surveyor instead of a farmer, to avoid repeating the farmers.

fr_taxe_noun.hook: Like English 'tax', said TAHKS: a box studded with round brass TACKS: everyone posts a coin into the TAX box.
fr_taxe_noun.why: Round-headed brass tacks, so nothing sharp is shown.

fr_interet_noun.hook: "an-tay-REH" ≈ "IN TRAY": coins hop into a wire IN-TRAY basket and multiply: INTEREST growing on savings.
fr_interet_noun.why: The in-tray is painted as a wire basket.

fr_economie_noun.hook: Like English "economy" (ay-koh-noh-MEE): a big clockwork model town on the floor (farm, factory and shop linked by turning gears, with a little toy train carrying coins between them): the whole ECONOMY at work.
fr_economie_noun.why: Owner asked for a better hook than the echoing piggy bank; the word is a cognate, so the picture now shows an economy itself.

fr_dette_noun.hook: "DEHT" ≈ "DEBT": a man drags a heavy ball and chain with a big blank slip tied on: his DEBT.
fr_dette_noun.why: The slip is blank (no IOU letters).

fr_faillite_noun.hook: "fah-YEET" ≈ "FAIL, YEET!": the little shop-box has tipped right over, spilling every coin, while the shopkeeper clutches his cheeks: BANKRUPTCY.
fr_faillite_noun.why: Repainted: no one throws anything now (owner disliked the coin-yeeting woman).

fr_opportunite_noun.hook: Like English 'opportunity', said oh-por-tew-nee-TAY: a little door opens a crack and a TEA cup waits on its step: OPPORTUNITY knocks.
fr_opportunite_noun.why: The teacup sits on the step of the open door.

fr_capitalisme_noun.hook: "ka-pi-ta-LEEZM" ≈ "CAP + CAPITAL": a factory owner in a flat CAP sits enthroned on a pyramid of gold coins: CAPITALISM.
fr_capitalisme_noun.why: Respelled the sound-out (the v1 spelling trips the content word filter); the picture is unchanged.

fr_capital_adj.hook: "ka-pi-TAHL" ≈ "CAP PETAL": a top-hat CAP brims with gold coins like PETALS: MAIN, of first importance, and CAPITAL money.
fr_capital_adj.why: The gold petals are painted as gold coins.

fr_subvention_noun.hook: "sewb-vahn-SYOHN" ≈ "SUB-INVENTION": a mayor hands a rolled GRANT to a girl beside her little brass submarine INVENTION.
fr_subvention_noun.why: A rolled grant scroll instead of a cheque, because the cheque already appears in the main hall.

fr_remboursement_noun.hook: "rahn-BOOR-suh-MAHN" ≈ "RAN BOURSE MAN": the BOURSE MAN RAN off with a little bag of coins to hand back a REFUND.
fr_remboursement_noun.why: Only the running man is painted.

fr_debouche_noun.hook: "day-boo-SHAY" ≈ "DAY, BOO-SHAY!": with a loud "BOOSH!" gold tumbles out of a brass pipe into the basket below: a new OUTLET, a market opening up.
fr_debouche_noun.why: No cork is painted; the gold pours straight out of the pipe.

fr_expertise_noun.hook: "ehk-spehr-TEEZ" ≈ "EXPERT TEASE": an EXPERT with a loupe APPRAISES a painting while a parrot on her shoulder TEASES her.
fr_expertise_noun.why: A parrot instead of a cat, to avoid repeating cats (the cat sits on the stock boxes).

fr_rentabilite_noun.hook: "RAHN-tah-BEE-lee-TAY" ≈ "RENT-a-BILLY": a farmer RENTS out his BILLY goat and a bucket of coins piles up: PROFITABILITY.
fr_rentabilite_noun.why: A billy goat instead of a beehive, because the bees already do le bilan.

fr_greve_noun.hook: "GREHV" ≈ "GRAVE": bank clerks with GRAVE faces fold their arms beside blank cardboard placards: they are ON STRIKE.
fr_greve_noun.why: Repainted: the placards are plain cardboard on sticks, no longer tombstone-shaped.

fr_crise_noun.hook: "KREEZ" ≈ "CREASE": a banker clutches his head over a chart CREASED down the middle: a CRISIS, everything crumpled.
fr_crise_noun.why: Repainted: the banker now has two arms (the old picture showed three).

fr_investissement_noun.hook: "an-VEHS-tee" ≈ "IN VEST": a girl tucks gold coins INTO her VEST pocket, then plants one as a seed in a flowerpot, where a green sprout comes up: an INVESTMENT.
fr_investissement_noun.why: Repainted: bare soil and one sprout, no coin-covered bush.

fr_benefice_noun.hook: "bay-nay-FEES" ≈ "BUNNY FEES": a plain brown BUNNY sits on the shelf beside a golden trophy brimming with coin FEES: the PROFIT pile.
fr_benefice_noun.why: Owner rule: the bunny IS the sound-alike, so it stays, but as a natural bunny (no apron, not standing like a person).

fr_compte_noun.hook: "KOHNT" ≈ "COUNT": a jolly old COUNT with a little gold coronet and a red sash licks his thumb to turn the pages of his bank ACCOUNT ledger at the lectern.
fr_compte_noun.why: The COUNT is the sound-alike, but the vampire costume was not: scary figures do not suit an all-ages bank, so he is now a friendly nobleman.
